nodes.label: Central Thesis
nodes.summary: Project-direction memory layer that keeps Codex work aligned with the original goal while allowing visible evolution.

nodes.label: Goal Anchor
nodes.summary: Stores the stable original project objective used as the reference point for later questions.

nodes.label: Baseline Structure
nodes.summary: Preserves the first coherent project structure so future changes can be compared against it.

nodes.label: Codex Wrapper
nodes.summary: Acts as the gateway that logs a question, loads direction context, prepares Codex context, and records outcomes.

nodes.label: Question Log
nodes.summary: Append-only log of meaningful user questions with stable ids and raw text.

nodes.label: Impact Analyzer
nodes.summary: Classifies whether a question is tactical, structural, direction-changing, drifting, conflicting, clarifying, or evidential.

nodes.label: Mental Model Delta
nodes.summary: Small explainable updates that record how a new question changes or strengthens the current model.

nodes.label: Context Capsule
nodes.summary: Compact project-direction context injected into Codex-facing work.

nodes.label: Mindmap Visualization
nodes.summary: Renders the current mental model, source questions, and recent deltas as a graph.

nodes.label: LLM Wiki Contrast
nodes.summary: Clarifies that the product tracks project direction changes, not just stored information retrieval.

nodes.label: Open Decisions
nodes.summary: Tracks unresolved product and architecture choices such as interface, storage, renderer, Codex integration depth, and compaction cadence.

nodes.label: External Runtime
nodes.summary: Supports using the wrapper outside the local browser by running a small local service or packaged desktop runtime that owns the .mental store and Codex task boundary.

nodes.label: Electron Shell
nodes.summary: Packages the mindmap UI and local wrapper service into a desktop app that can stay open without relying on a browser tab.

nodes.label: Codex Execution Adapter
nodes.summary: Defines how prepared context capsules are handed to Codex CLI/API and how outcomes return to the mental model logs.

nodes.label: Installable Codex-like CLI
nodes.summary: The product should be installable like Codex and expose a command that opens or attaches to a project workspace.

nodes.label: Mindmap-first Launch
nodes.summary: Running the installed wrapper should open the project mindmap first, making the current mental model the default surface before development continues.

nodes.label: Development Activity Capture
nodes.summary: Codex-like development actions should feed question logs, decisions, outcomes, and model deltas so the mindmap is drawn as work happens.

nodes.label: Question Direction Directive
nodes.summary: Captures explicit # directives before Codex questions so the user controls whether a task is directionless, weakly structural, strongly directional, boundary-setting, conflicting, drifting, or evidential.

nodes.label: Project Workspace Analysis
nodes.summary: goal-graph: Monorepo, Node.js, TypeScript; source directories: apps, packages, tests; docs: AGENTS.md, README.md, package.json.

nodes.label: Terminal Session Runtime
nodes.summary: Running the installed command without a subcommand opens the current workspace, asks for consent if needed, analyzes the project, then keeps a terminal prompt for questions, mode changes, sync, and exit.

edges.summary: The current thesis must stay comparable to the original Goal Anchor.
Current structure is interpreted against the first baseline structure.
The wrapper logs meaningful user questions before preparing Codex work.
Question events feed deterministic impact analysis.
Impact analysis produces small mental model deltas.
Deltas update the compact context used by Codex-facing tasks.
The visible mindmap reflects the current model and recent direction deltas.
The Goal Anchor prevents the product from collapsing into a generic LLM wiki.
The wrapper should be usable as a local runtime outside a browser-only flow.
Electron is the preferred desktop shell for keeping the wrapper UI open without a browser tab.
The wrapper needs an adapter boundary for handing context-rich tasks to Codex and capturing outcomes.
The Electron shell hosts the mindmap UI while the local runtime updates the graph files.
The installed CLI starts or attaches to the local external runtime for a workspace.
The first visible result of running the tool should be the project mindmap.
The Codex adapter captures task input and outcome so development activity updates the mental model.
Captured development activity refreshes the mindmap graph continuously.
Electron hosts the always-on mindmap-first experience without requiring a browser tab.
The raw question is logged with normalized text and directive metadata while preserving source text.
The directive overrides or constrains heuristic impact analysis before model deltas are produced.
#none questions should not refresh direction context as structural changes, while #strong questions should force an explicit delta.
Project analysis is compacted into context before wrapped Codex work continues.
The installed command starts an always-on terminal prompt when run without a subcommand.
The terminal session checks for .mental, asks consent when missing, and analyzes the workspace before normal questions continue.
The terminal session exposes .sync so refreshed graph and log artifacts stay aligned with the current model.

open_questions: Initial storage: local files only, SQLite, PostgreSQL, or graph DB?
Mindmap renderer: React Flow, Cytoscape.js, Mermaid, or custom canvas?
Codex integration depth: context injection only, CLI execution, MCP integration, or full orchestration?
How often should the model be compacted or re-summarized?
Electron desktop shell details: tray behavior, auto-start, workspace picker, and packaged Codex execution boundary.
External runtime mode: local service, CLI-only, Electron-bundled service, or MCP server.
How should the installed command attach to Codex: wrap Codex CLI directly, launch Codex as a child process, or integrate through API/MCP?
Which default mode should the installed app use for new users: auto, none, or a guided prompt?
How much project analysis should run automatically before asking the user for more project intent?
Should the interactive terminal session execute Codex directly next, or continue preparing prompts until the CodexExecutionAdapter is hardened?
active_decisions: Use local file storage for the MVP before introducing a database.
Use TypeScript and Node.js for core logic.
Expose a CLI wrapper before full Codex orchestration.
Prefer an Electron desktop shell as the always-on UI while preserving CLI/local service usage for external environments.
The target external usage is install -> run -> mindmap opens -> Codex-like development continuously updates the mindmap.
Question impact is controlled by # directives or the workspace default question mode before Codex execution.
Terminal open flow analyzes the current workspace before normal wrapped Codex questions.
Running goal-graph without a subcommand opens an interactive terminal session for the current workspace.
risks: The wrapper may degrade into a generic history viewer if impact analysis and source-question traceability are weak.
The mindmap may become decorative if recent direction changes are not visible.
Codex integration depth is still unresolved.
Electron packaging can blur UI, local service, and Codex execution responsibilities unless the execution adapter boundary stays explicit.
The product will fail the target experience if users must manually sync logs or open a separate browser to see the mindmap.
Without explicit question directives, tactical Codex work can pollute direction history and make the mindmap noisy.
Project analysis can become noisy if generated evidence is treated as a user direction without consent.
